$comment: Generic rules shipped with the operating-model plugin. A project adds its own, or disables one of these by id, in <project>/.claude/guard-rules.json. Format: README.md beside this file. guard-bash-command.py embeds an identical copy (EMBEDDED_RULES), used if this file is missing or invalid; change both together.

rules.message: `gh pr merge --auto` is refused: in a repository whose default branch has no required status checks, --auto merges at once, before CI finishes. Safe form: watch the checks (`gh pr checks <pr> --watch`), then merge explicitly (`gh pr merge <pr> --squash`). A project that does require checks can turn this rule off in .claude/guard-rules.json.

This command prints a Vault or OpenBao token itself: `token lookup`, `print token`, and a `read` or `write` of `auth/token/lookup`, `lookup-self` or `lookup-accessor` without a `-field=` (other than `id`) placed before the path. Safe form: read one field, with the flag before the path, for example `bao read -field=ttl auth/token/lookup-self` (other fields: policies, display_name, expire_time).
